learning_outcomes.text: Analyze, reason, and develop individually and as a team different solutions for machine elements that satisfy specific needs or objective functions.

syllabus_topics: Synthesis of the four-bar linkage mechanism
Synthesis of the Maltese cross mechanism
Machine stability. Stable and unstable machines
Verification of engine balancing and machine irregularity
Machine dynamics using computer-aided engineering tools
Theoretical design of clutches and brakes
Verification of an automobile brake and an internal combustion engine clutch
Theoretical design of a cam transmission
Theoretical design of a gear transmission
Theoretical design of a transmission using gear trains
Kinematic analysis of an epicyclic gear train, reducer, manual gearbox and differential
Theoretical design of a transmission using belts
teaching_methods: Seminars or problem classes or practical cases

assessment_methods.method: Lab practices utilization (average score from booklets)
Resolution and submission of practical activities (cases, problems, reports, projects)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary continuous assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.70 * Final Exam + 0.20 * Lab Practices + 0.10 * Practical Activities. A minimum score of 5 on the Final Exam is required to pass the subject. If the Final Exam score is less than 5, the final grade will be the calculated sum if less than 5, or 4 otherwise. Lab Practices and Practical Activities from the ordinary call are not recoverable. For the extraordinary call and global evaluation, the weighting is 0.80 * Final Exam + 0.20 * Lab Practices (or Lab Practices Exam for global evaluation), with the same minimum score rule for the Final Exam and the same grade capping if the exam is failed.
